additional_info.subject: Handover notes
additional_info.body:
The customer complains:
On August 27, 2025, a personal acquaintance tried three times to
log in at the station in Chavannes, unfortunately without success. I
followed the process by phone. Despite trying two different credit
cards, the transaction could not be completed.
Details:
• Connector: A1
• EVSE ID: CH*ECUE4FVLU244V4BUGAXX2Z4SEZDDUQ
• Date: 08/27/2025
• Time: approx. 4:30–4:35 p.m.
• Observation: The circle on the screen kept spinning endlessly, and
despite several attempts with two different credit cards, charging
was not possible.
Could you please check your logs to investigate the incident? The
aim is to understand whether this was a short-term technical glitch
or whether there is room for improvement in communication.

additional_info.subject: 0447574 - ID0447574-DC/Si-D/CH-[MP / R7 170002201] transaction issue CRM:00472000374
additional_info.body:
Dear Alexander,
Our analysis of the recent logs indicates a communication failure between the charger and the CCV payment terminal. The specific error message observed in the logs is:
{"errno":-113,"code":"EHOSTUNREACH","syscall":"connect","address":"10.20.17.50" ...}
, which points to an inability to reach the payment terminal's IP address.
To resolve this issue, please schedule an onsite intervention and perform the following diagnostic steps:
Payment Terminal Inspection:
Verify the integrity and correct connection of the Ethernet cable. Please test with an alternative cable to rule out any cable-related issues.
Inspect the LEDs on the back of the payment terminal to ensure that tamper mode is not active.
Network Connectivity Check:
Connect your laptop directly to the charger's network switch.
Perform a network scan to determine if the IP address
10.20.17.50
is reachable from this point.
Component Replacement (Conditional):
If the IP address
10.20.17.50
cannot be found or reached during the network scan, please proceed with the replacement of the CCV payment terminal.
With best regards,
Joao Francisco Louro Cardoso
Siemens S.A.
SI E CS SD L3
201, Avenida 25 de Abril
2845-547 Corroios, Portugal
mailto:joao.louro-cardoso@siemens.com

additional_info.subject: 0447574 - ID0447574-DC/Si-D/CH-[MP / R7 170002201] transaction issue CRM:00472000376
additional_info.body:
Dear Alexander,
Initially, based on the attached report indicating the client's attempt to use two different credit cards and the charger's configuration for CCV payment terminal (which requires verification for accuracy), my focus was on a potential credit card transaction problem.
However, upon further review, I identified a critical detail I had previously overlooked: the authentication methods for the outlets do not include credit card payments.
A subsequent, more thorough examination of the logs revealed additional insights:
Remote start attempts, presumably initiated by the client via the application, did not correspond to the connector ID to which the vehicle was physically connected.
A later attempt by the user to initiate another remote start transaction for Connector ID 2 was rejected. This rejection occurred because there was already a pending transaction accepted for that plug, awaiting an EV connection.
Based on these observations, it appears that the issue is likely a user misunderstanding or operational error rather than a malfunction of the charger itself.
Nevertheless, I recommend verifying the overall functionality of remote start transactions initiated via the application to ensure seamless user experience.
Should you require any further details or clarification, please do not hesitate to contact me via the ticketing system or Microsoft Teams.
I await your approval to close this ticket, as there are no further actions required from our end following this explanation.
With best regards,
Joao Francisco Louro Cardoso
Siemens S.A.
